description: Reading and writing MAT-files, delimited text and spreadsheets, low-level binary and formatted file access, JSON, XML, HDF5 and netCDF scientific formats, web service calls, and image, audio and video files. These functions are how MATLAB exchanges data with the rest of the world.

tools.name: load
tools.description: Loads variables from a MAT-file into the workspace, or reads a whitespace-delimited numeric text file into a matrix. Assigning the result to a variable returns a structure with one field per stored variable, which is far safer than letting load create workspace variables implicitly. Use the variable list arguments to load only what you need from a large file.
tools.usage:
load(filename)
S = load(filename)
S = load(filename, variables)
load(filename, '-mat')
load(filename, '-ascii')

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: MAT-file or text file to read.

parameters.name: variables
parameters.description: Names or regular expressions (with '-regexp') selecting variables to load.

parameters.name: '-mat'/'-ascii'
parameters.description: Force interpretation as a MAT-file or as numeric text.

tools.notes: Bare `load` silently overwrites existing workspace variables and makes code hard to analyse; always capture the output struct in functions. `matfile` loads parts of large v7.3 files without reading everything.

tools.name: save
tools.description: Saves workspace variables to a MAT-file, with options for the file version, compression and appending. Version 7.3 uses HDF5 and is required for variables larger than 2 GB and for partial loading with `matfile`. Use it to checkpoint results, cache expensive computations and pass data between sessions.
tools.usage:
save(filename)
save(filename, variables)
save(filename, variables, '-append')
save(filename, '-v7.3')
save(filename, '-struct', 'S')

parameters.name: variables
parameters.description: Names of variables to save; all workspace variables by default.

parameters.name: '-append'
parameters.description: Add to an existing file instead of replacing it.

parameters.name: '-nocompression'
parameters.description: Skip compression for faster saving of already-compact data.

parameters.name: '-struct'
parameters.description: Save the fields of a struct as separate variables.

tools.notes: Compression costs time on save and load; '-nocompression' can be much faster for large numeric arrays. Use the functional form `save(fname, varname)` when the file name is in a variable.

tools.name: matfile
tools.description: Creates an object that accesses variables inside a MAT-file without loading the whole file into memory, supporting indexed reads and writes of parts of arrays. Use it for data sets larger than RAM, for appending to results incrementally, and for reading a slice of a big array. Partial access requires a version 7.3 file.
tools.usage:
m = matfile(filename)
m = matfile(filename, 'Writable', true)
data = m.varName(rows, cols)
m.varName(rows, cols) = data

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: MAT-file to open; created if it does not exist and Writable is true.

parameters.name: 'Writable'
parameters.description: true to allow writing; false by default.

tools.notes: Partial loading only works on v7.3 files; older versions load the entire variable behind the scenes. Indexing a matfile object in a tight loop is slow because each access hits the disk, so read in blocks.

tools.name: readmatrix
tools.description: Reads numeric data from a delimited text file or spreadsheet into a matrix, skipping headers automatically. Use it when the file is purely numeric and you do not need variable names or mixed types. It is the modern replacement for `csvread`, `dlmread` and numeric `xlsread`.
tools.usage:
A = readmatrix(filename)
A = readmatrix(filename, Name, Value)
A = readmatrix(filename, opts)

parameters.name: 'Range'
parameters.description: Cell range or row/column range to read.

parameters.name: 'NumHeaderLines'
parameters.description: Lines to skip before the data.

parameters.name: 'OutputType'
parameters.description: Class of the result, for example 'double', 'single', 'string'.

tools.notes: Non-numeric cells become NaN. If your file has labels or mixed types, use `readtable` or `readcell` instead so nothing is silently lost.

tools.name: writematrix
tools.description: Writes a matrix to a delimited text file or spreadsheet, without variable names or row labels. Use it for simple numeric exports that other tools will parse. The extension of the file name determines the format.
tools.usage:
writematrix(A)
writematrix(A, filename)
writematrix(A, filename, Name, Value)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Output file; extension selects the format.

tools.notes: Numbers are written with enough digits to round-trip for double precision. To include headers, build a table and use `writetable` instead.

tools.name: readcell
tools.description: Reads a file into a cell array, preserving mixed types cell by cell so that text and numbers coexist. Use it for ragged or irregular files where neither a matrix nor a table fits, and for inspecting a file's raw structure before deciding how to import it. Missing values appear as the missing value of the corresponding type.
tools.usage:
C = readcell(filename)
C = readcell(filename, Name, Value)
C = readcell(filename, opts)
tools.notes: Empty cells become `missing` rather than empty strings. `writecell` performs the reverse export.

tools.name: writecell
tools.description: Writes a cell array to a delimited text file or spreadsheet, converting each cell to text as needed. Use it to export heterogeneous data assembled in a cell array without first building a table. Formatting options match those of `writematrix` and `writetable`.
tools.usage:
writecell(C)
writecell(C, filename)
writecell(C, filename, Name, Value)
tools.notes: Cells containing arrays or objects that cannot be converted to text cause an error. For consistent typed columns, prefer a table and `writetable`.

tools.name: readlines
tools.description: Reads a text file into a string array with one element per line, handling encoding and line endings automatically. Use it for log files, configuration files and any line-oriented text you want to process with string functions. It is simpler and faster than a fopen/fgetl loop.
tools.usage:
str = readlines(filename)
str = readlines(filename, Name, Value)
tools.notes: Available since R2020b. For very large files, a `fopen`/`fgetl` loop or a `datastore` avoids loading everything into memory at once.

tools.name: writelines
tools.description: Writes a string array to a text file, one element per line, with control over encoding, line endings and whether to append. Use it to emit generated code, configuration files and reports without managing file handles. It is the counterpart of `readlines`.
tools.usage:
writelines(lines, filename)
writelines(lines, filename, Name, Value)

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: String array, character vector or cellstr to write.

parameters.name: 'TrailingLineEnding'
parameters.description: Whether to end the last line with a terminator.

tools.notes: Available since R2022a. On Windows the default line ending is CRLF; set 'LineEnding' to "\n" when the consumer expects Unix endings.

tools.name: readstruct
tools.description: Reads an XML or JSON file into a MATLAB structure, mapping elements and attributes to fields. Use it as the quick way to consume configuration and data files in those formats without manual DOM traversal. `writestruct` writes a structure back out.
tools.usage:
S = readstruct(filename)
S = readstruct(filename, Name, Value)
writestruct(S, filename)

parameters.name: 'FileType'
parameters.description: 'xml' or 'json' when the extension is ambiguous.

parameters.name: 'AttributeSuffix'
parameters.description: Suffix appended to field names created from XML attributes.

tools.notes: Available since R2020b. Repeated XML elements become struct arrays. For full control over an XML document tree, use `xmlread` and the DOM interface.

tools.name: fileread
tools.description: Reads an entire text file into a single character vector, including newline characters. Use it when you want to apply regular expressions to a whole file at once, or to hash or compare file contents. For line-by-line work, `readlines` gives a more convenient structure.
tools.usage:
chr = fileread(filename)
chr = fileread(filename, 'Encoding', enc)
tools.notes: The whole file is held in memory, so avoid it for very large files. It reads in text mode, so line endings are returned as they appear in the file.

tools.name: textscan
tools.description: Reads formatted data from a text file or character vector according to a format specification, returning a cell array with one element per conversion. It handles mixed numeric and text columns, custom delimiters, comment lines and blocks of a chosen number of rows. Use it for large or awkward text files that `readtable` cannot parse cleanly.
tools.usage:
C = textscan(fid, formatSpec)
C = textscan(fid, formatSpec, N)
C = textscan(chr, formatSpec)
C = textscan(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: fid
parameters.description: File identifier from `fopen`, or a character vector to parse.

parameters.name: formatSpec
parameters.description: Conversion specifiers such as %f, %d, %s, %q, %*s to skip, and literal text.

parameters.name: N
parameters.description: Number of times to apply the format; Inf for the whole file.

parameters.name: 'HeaderLines'
parameters.description: Lines to skip at the start.

parameters.name: 'TreatAsEmpty'
parameters.description: Text to treat as an empty numeric field.

parameters.name: 'CollectOutput'
parameters.description: true to group consecutive same-type outputs into one array.

tools.notes: textscan stops at the first line that does not match the format, which silently truncates the result; check how many rows you got. It leaves the file position where it stopped, so it can be called repeatedly to read in blocks.

tools.name: detectImportOptions
tools.description: Analyses a text, spreadsheet, XML or fixed-width file and returns an import options object describing variable names, types, ranges and rules for missing and erroneous values. Modify the object and pass it to `readtable`, `readmatrix` or `readcell` for precise, repeatable imports. Use it whenever automatic detection guesses a type wrongly.
tools.usage:
opts = detectImportOptions(filename)
opts = detectImportOptions(filename, Name, Value)
opts = setvartype(opts, vars, type)
opts = setvaropts(opts, vars, Name, Value)
tools.notes: Type detection samples only the first rows of large files, so a column that turns numeric only later may be read as text. Saving the options object makes an import reproducible across releases.

tools.name: importdata
tools.description: Loads data from a wide range of file types, guessing the format and returning either an array or a structure with data, text and header fields. Use it for a quick first look at an unfamiliar file. For production code, the specific readers give predictable results and better control.
tools.usage:
A = importdata(filename)
A = importdata(filename, delimiterIn)
A = importdata(filename, delimiterIn, headerlinesIn)
[A, delimiterOut, headerlinesOut] = importdata(___)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: File of almost any supported type: text, spreadsheet, image, audio, MAT.

parameters.name: headerlinesIn
parameters.description: Number of header lines to skip.

tools.notes: The return type varies with the file content, so code that uses importdata must check with `isstruct` before indexing. Prefer `readtable`, `readmatrix` or `imread` when you know the format.

tools.name: fopen
tools.description: Opens a file and returns a file identifier used by the low-level I/O functions, or -1 if the open fails. The permission string selects reading, writing, appending, text or binary mode and update access. Always check the identifier and capture the error message before reading or writing.
tools.usage:
fid = fopen(filename)
fid = fopen(filename, permission)
fid = fopen(filename, permission, machinefmt, encoding)
[fid, errmsg] = fopen(___)
fids = fopen('all')

parameters.name: permission
parameters.description: 'r', 'w', 'a', 'r+', 'w+', 'a+', optionally with 't' for text or 'b' for binary.

tools.notes: Every successful fopen must be matched by an `fclose`; wrapping the close in an `onCleanup` object guarantees it even if an error occurs. File identifiers 1 and 2 are standard output and standard error and must never be closed.

tools.name: fclose
tools.description: Closes an open file, flushing any buffered output and releasing the file identifier. Call it for every file you open, or use `onCleanup` so it happens even when an error interrupts the function. Passing 'all' closes every open file, which is useful for cleaning up after a failed script.
tools.usage:
fclose(fid)
fclose('all')
status = fclose(___)
tools.notes: Data written with `fprintf` or `fwrite` may still be buffered until the file is closed, so a reader running concurrently may see nothing. A status of 0 means success and -1 means failure.

tools.name: fprintf
tools.description: Writes formatted text to a file or, when no file identifier is given, to the command window. The format string is reapplied until all data is consumed, which makes it easy to write whole arrays. Use it for logging, for progress messages and for writing formatted text data files.
tools.usage:
fprintf(formatSpec, A1, ..., An)
fprintf(fid, formatSpec, A1, ..., An)
nbytes = fprintf(___)

parameters.name: fid
parameters.description: File identifier; 1 is standard output and 2 is standard error.

parameters.name: formatSpec
parameters.description: Format string with conversion specifications and escape sequences.

tools.notes: Arrays are consumed in column-major order, so writing rows of a matrix usually requires transposing it first. A literal percent sign is written as %%.

tools.name: fscanf
tools.description: Reads formatted numeric or text data from a file according to a format specification, returning the values in column order. Use it for regular numeric files where every record has the same layout. It fills the output in column-major order, so a size argument is usually needed followed by a transpose.
tools.usage:
A = fscanf(fid, formatSpec)
A = fscanf(fid, formatSpec, sizeA)
[A, count] = fscanf(___)

parameters.name: sizeA
parameters.description: Output size: Inf, n, or [m n].

tools.notes: fscanf stops at the first item that does not match, so check the count output. `textscan` is more flexible for mixed and irregular data.

tools.name: fgetl
tools.description: Reads the next line from a file and returns it without the line terminator, or -1 at end of file. Use it in a while loop to process a text file line by line without loading it all into memory. The sibling `fgets` keeps the terminator.
tools.usage: tline = fgetl(fid)
tools.notes: The end-of-file marker is the numeric -1, so test with `~ischar(tline)` rather than comparing to -1, which would fail on a line that happens to read as a number. An empty line returns an empty character vector, not -1.

tools.name: fread
tools.description: Reads binary data from a file and converts it to a MATLAB class, with control over the source precision, skip intervals and byte order. Use it for raw instrument data, custom binary formats and byte-level file inspection. The precision string can specify a source type and a different output type.
tools.usage:
A = fread(fid)
A = fread(fid, sizeA)
A = fread(fid, sizeA, precision)
A = fread(fid, sizeA, precision, skip)
[A, count] = fread(___)

parameters.name: sizeA
parameters.description: Inf, n, or [m n] describing how much to read and the output shape.

parameters.name: precision
parameters.description: Source type such as 'uint8', 'int16', 'double', or 'int16=>double' to control the output class.

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Bytes to skip after each element, for reading interleaved data.

tools.notes: Without the => notation, integer data is returned as double, which can quadruple memory use. Byte order is set in `fopen`; mismatched endianness produces plausible but wrong numbers.

tools.name: fwrite
tools.description: Writes binary data to a file in a specified precision, optionally skipping bytes between elements. Use it to produce raw binary files for other programs, to write custom headers, and to stream numeric data compactly. Data is written in column-major order.
tools.usage:
fwrite(fid, A)
fwrite(fid, A, precision)
fwrite(fid, A, precision, skip)
count = fwrite(___)

parameters.name: skip
parameters.description: Bytes to skip after each element.

tools.notes: Values that do not fit the target precision are saturated, not wrapped. Specify the byte order in `fopen` when the file will be read on another platform.

tools.name: feof
tools.description: Tests whether the end-of-file indicator has been set for an open file, returning 1 after a read has attempted to go past the end. Use it as a loop condition when reading a file sequentially. Note that it reports the state after the last read, not whether the next read will succeed.
tools.usage: status = feof(fid)
tools.notes: Because feof becomes true only after a read fails, a naive `while ~feof` loop can process one extra iteration; guard the value you read as in the example. `ferror` reports the reason a read failed.

tools.name: fseek
tools.description: Moves the file position indicator to a byte offset relative to the beginning, the current position or the end of the file. Use it to skip headers, to read a record at a known offset, and to rewind for a second pass. `ftell` reports the current position and `frewind` returns to the start.
tools.usage:
status = fseek(fid, offset, origin)
pos = ftell(fid)
frewind(fid)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of bytes to move; may be negative.

tools.notes: Seeking in text mode on Windows can be unreliable because of line-ending translation; open with 'rb' for byte-accurate positioning. A status of 0 means success.

tools.name: jsonencode
tools.description: Converts MATLAB data to a JSON text string, mapping structs to objects, cell arrays and numeric arrays to arrays, and strings to JSON strings. Use it to build request bodies for web services and to write configuration and result files. The PrettyPrint option makes output human readable.
tools.usage:
text = jsonencode(data)
text = jsonencode(data, 'ConvertInfAndNaN', tf)
text = jsonencode(data, 'PrettyPrint', true)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Struct, array, cell, table, string, logical or numeric value.

parameters.name: 'ConvertInfAndNaN'
parameters.description: true (default) writes Inf and NaN as null; false writes them literally.

tools.notes: Field names that are not valid JSON keys are written as-is, and MATLAB's `matlab.lang.makeValidName` mangling is not reversed. A 1-by-N numeric array becomes a JSON array, but a scalar struct field holding a 1-element array also becomes a one-element array, which can surprise strict consumers.

tools.name: jsondecode
tools.description: Parses JSON text into MATLAB data, producing structs for objects, numeric arrays for homogeneous arrays and cell arrays for heterogeneous ones. Use it to consume web service responses and configuration files. Object keys that are not valid MATLAB identifiers are modified to become field names.
tools.usage: data = jsondecode(text)

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: JSON text as a character vector or string.

tools.notes: An array of objects with identical keys becomes a struct array, but if the keys differ it becomes a cell array of structs, so downstream code must handle both shapes. JSON null becomes an empty array.

tools.name: webread
tools.description: Sends an HTTP GET request and returns the response, automatically decoding JSON, text, images, tables and audio based on the content type. Query parameters can be given as name-value pairs after the URL. Use it as the simplest way to call a REST API from MATLAB.
tools.usage:
data = webread(url)
data = webread(url, QueryName1, QueryValue1, ...)
data = webread(url, options)
data = webread(url, QueryName1, QueryValue1, ..., options)

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `weboptions` object controlling timeout, headers, authentication and content type.

tools.notes: Query values are URL-encoded automatically, so do not encode them yourself. Never place credentials in the URL; use the Username, Password or HeaderFields options of `weboptions` instead.

tools.name: webwrite
tools.description: Sends an HTTP POST request with data in the body and returns the decoded response. Name-value pairs are sent as form data by default, or as JSON when the MediaType option says so. Use it to submit forms and call REST endpoints that create or modify resources.
tools.usage:
response = webwrite(url, PostName1, PostValue1, ...)
response = webwrite(url, data)
response = webwrite(url, ___, options)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Character vector or string sent as the raw body.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `weboptions` object; set MediaType to 'application/json' for JSON bodies.

tools.notes: For PUT, DELETE or PATCH, or for fine control over headers and multipart bodies, use the `matlab.net.http` package instead. webwrite always uses POST.

tools.name: websave
tools.description: Downloads the content at a URL directly to a file and returns the full path of the saved file. Use it for fetching data sets, model files and archives without loading them into memory first. Query parameters and `weboptions` work as they do for `webread`.
tools.usage:
outfilename = websave(filename, url)
outfilename = websave(filename, url, QueryName1, QueryValue1, ...)
outfilename = websave(filename, url, options)

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: `weboptions` object with Timeout, HeaderFields and credentials.

tools.notes: The file is overwritten without warning if it already exists. Large downloads need a generous Timeout, because the default of 5 seconds applies to the whole transfer.

tools.name: weboptions
tools.description: Creates an options object that configures HTTP requests made by `webread`, `webwrite` and `websave`: timeouts, headers, authentication, content and media types, certificate files and proxies. Use it whenever the default 5-second timeout or automatic content detection is not right. The object can be reused across many calls.
tools.usage:
options = weboptions
options = weboptions(Name, Value, ...)

parameters.name: 'Timeout'
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the whole request; default 5.

parameters.name: 'HeaderFields'
parameters.description: N-by-2 cell array of extra request headers.

parameters.name: 'CertificateFilename'
parameters.description: Path to a CA bundle, or '' to skip verification.

tools.notes: Setting CertificateFilename to '' disables TLS certificate verification and should only be used against trusted internal hosts. Prefer token headers over Username/Password when the API supports them.

tools.name: xmlread
tools.description: Parses an XML file into a Document Object Model tree that can be traversed and queried with the standard DOM methods. Use it when you need full control over namespaces, attributes and mixed content that `readstruct` cannot express. `xmlwrite` serializes a DOM back to text.
tools.usage:
DOMnode = xmlread(filename)
chr = xmlwrite(DOMnode)
xmlwrite(filename, DOMnode)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: XML file, URL or input source.

tools.notes: The DOM interface is Java-based, so it needs the JVM and returns Java objects that usually need `char` conversion. For simple structured files, `readstruct` is far less verbose.

tools.name: h5read
tools.description: Reads a data set, or a hyperslab of one, from an HDF5 file. Use it for large scientific data sets where you need to read only a region, and for exchanging data with tools built on HDF5. `h5info` inspects the file structure and `h5disp` prints it.
tools.usage:
data = h5read(filename, ds)
data = h5read(filename, ds, start, count)
data = h5read(filename, ds, start, count, stride)

parameters.name: ds
parameters.description: Full path of the data set inside the file, for example '/group/dataset'.

parameters.name: start, count, stride
parameters.description: One-based start index, number of elements and stride per dimension.

tools.notes: HDF5 indexing here is one-based like MATLAB, unlike the underlying C library. MAT-file version 7.3 files are HDF5, so h5 functions can inspect them, though the internal layout is MathWorks specific.

tools.name: h5write
tools.description: Writes data to a data set in an HDF5 file, either the whole set or a hyperslab. The data set must already exist, created with `h5create`, which fixes its dimensions, type and chunking. Use it for incremental writing of large arrays and for producing files other scientific tools can read.
tools.usage:
h5write(filename, ds, data)
h5write(filename, ds, data, start, count)
h5write(filename, ds, data, start, count, stride)

parameters.name: ds
parameters.description: Path of the target data set.

tools.notes: Unlimited dimensions require a ChunkSize in `h5create`. Writing a type different from the one declared at creation raises an error, so create with the intended Datatype.

tools.name: ncread
tools.description: Reads a variable, or part of one, from a netCDF file, applying scale factor and offset attributes automatically. netCDF is the standard format for climate, ocean and atmospheric data, so this is the entry point for most geophysical data sets. `ncinfo` and `ncdisp` reveal the variables, dimensions and attributes.
tools.usage:
vardata = ncread(source, varname)
vardata = ncread(source, varname, start, count)
vardata = ncread(source, varname, start, count, stride)

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: netCDF file name or an OPeNDAP URL.

parameters.name: varname
parameters.description: Name of the variable to read.

parameters.name: start, count, stride
parameters.description: One-based start, element count and stride per dimension.

tools.notes: ncread applies scale_factor and add_offset by default; use `ncreadatt` to inspect them. Reading from an OPeNDAP URL fetches only the requested hyperslab over the network.

tools.name: ncwrite
tools.description: Writes data to a variable in a netCDF file, creating the file and variable first with `nccreate` if needed. Use it to produce standards-compliant data files for geoscience workflows and to append along an unlimited dimension. Attributes are written separately with `ncwriteatt`.
tools.usage:
ncwrite(filename, varname, vardata)
ncwrite(filename, varname, vardata, start)
ncwrite(filename, varname, vardata, start, stride)

parameters.name: start, stride
parameters.description: One-based start index and stride for partial writes.

tools.notes: Only the last dimension may be unlimited in the classic netCDF model. Writing past the declared size of a fixed dimension raises an error.

tools.name: imread
tools.description: Reads an image from a file into an array, returning uint8, uint16 or double data depending on the format, plus an optional colormap and alpha channel. It supports PNG, JPEG, TIFF, GIF, BMP, HDF, and many other formats. Use it to load images for processing, display and analysis.
tools.usage:
A = imread(filename)
A = imread(filename, fmt)
[A, map] = imread(___)
[A, map, alpha] = imread(___)
A = imread(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: fmt
parameters.description: Format extension when the file name lacks one.

parameters.name: 'Index'
parameters.description: Frame to read from a multi-image file such as GIF or TIFF.

parameters.name: 'PixelRegion'
parameters.description: Region to read from large TIFF files.

tools.notes: Indexed images return data plus a colormap; convert with `ind2rgb`. Arithmetic on uint8 images saturates, so convert to double before scaling. `imfinfo` reads metadata without decoding the pixels.

tools.name: imwrite
tools.description: Writes an array to an image file, choosing the format from the extension or an explicit format argument. Format-specific options control JPEG quality, PNG bit depth, TIFF compression and GIF animation. Use it to export processed images and generated graphics rasters.
tools.usage:
imwrite(A, filename)
imwrite(A, map, filename)
imwrite(___, fmt)
imwrite(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Image data; uint8, uint16, logical or double in [0,1].

parameters.name: 'WriteMode'
parameters.description: 'overwrite' or 'append' for multi-page TIFF and GIF.

tools.notes: Double image data must be scaled to [0,1] or it is clipped. To save a figure rather than an image array, use `exportgraphics`, which captures axes, labels and annotations.

tools.name: audioread
tools.description: Reads an audio file into a sample matrix with one column per channel, plus the sample rate. Supported formats include WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3 and MPEG-4 AAC. Use it to load sound for analysis, filtering and playback, optionally reading only a range of samples.
tools.usage:
[y, Fs] = audioread(filename)
[y, Fs] = audioread(filename, samples)
[y, Fs] = audioread(___, dataType)
tools.notes: The default double output is normalized to [-1,1] regardless of the file's bit depth; use 'native' to get the raw integer samples. `audioinfo` reads duration and channel count without decoding.

tools.name: audiowrite
tools.description: Writes audio samples to a file at a given sample rate, with the format chosen from the extension. Options control bit depth, quality for compressed formats and metadata such as title and artist. Use it to export synthesized or processed audio.
tools.usage:
audiowrite(filename, y, Fs)
audiowrite(filename, y, Fs, Name, Value)

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: Sample matrix with one column per channel.

parameters.name: 'Quality'
parameters.description: 0 to 100 for compressed formats such as MP4/M4A.

tools.notes: Samples outside [-1,1] are clipped for double input. WAV and FLAC support 24-bit output, while MP4 uses the Quality option instead of a bit depth.

tools.name: VideoReader
tools.description: Creates an object for reading video files frame by frame, exposing properties such as Duration, FrameRate, Height, Width and NumFrames. Use `readFrame` with `hasFrame` to stream sequentially, or `read` to fetch specific frame numbers. It supports the codecs installed on the host platform.
tools.usage:
v = VideoReader(filename)
v = VideoReader(filename, Name, Value)
frame = readFrame(v)
tf = hasFrame(v)
frames = read(v, index)

parameters.name: 'CurrentTime'
parameters.description: Time in seconds at which to start reading.

tools.notes: NumFrames may require scanning the whole file for some formats and can be slow or approximate. Sequential reading with readFrame is much faster than repeated random access with read.

tools.name: VideoWriter
tools.description: Creates an object for writing video files, with a choice of profiles such as 'MPEG-4', 'Motion JPEG AVI', 'Archival' and 'Uncompressed AVI'. Open it, write frames or figure snapshots, then close it. Use it to record animations and simulation results.
tools.usage:
v = VideoWriter(filename)
v = VideoWriter(filename, profile)
open(v)
writeVideo(v, frame)
close(v)

parameters.name: v.FrameRate
parameters.description: Frames per second; set before opening.

tools.notes: Properties such as FrameRate and Quality can only be set before `open`. Always `close` the writer or the file will be unusable; wrap it in `onCleanup` for safety. MPEG-4 requires frame dimensions that are even numbers.
